3) PV strategy: block vs. object and encryption/key management (15 min)

Notes up-front:
- We typically recommend separate node pools for inference (low-latency, GPU-attached) and batch (preemptible / lower-cost CPU pools).
- For model artifacts, we prefer S3-compatible object storage with an NFS/CSI cache for hot model pulls; block PVs for user-tenant writeable data with encryption at rest.
- Tenant isolation depends on trust boundaries: strongly regulated tenants often warrant cluster-per-tenant; otherwise namespaced multi-tenant with strict RBAC and network policies is typical.

Quick reference before tomorrow's call — pulled from our standard on-prem sizing playbook. Summary bullets for the call:

Node profiles (example for GroundTruth 3-rack site):
- inference-gpu-pool (rack spread): 8x A100-equivalent per rack, 1 pod per GPU, node allocatable set to preserve 10% RAM headroom. Use isolated SELinux profile and dedicated taints (redwood.inference=dedicated:NoSchedule).
- burst-cpu-pool: mixed 64vCPU, 256GB RAM nodes for large preprocessing jobs; use preemptible lower-cost policy for non-critical batch.
- infra-pool: 3x control-plane adjacent nodes (no GPUs) for logging/metrics/control plane proxies; recommend HA across racks.

Storage recommendations:
- Model artifacts: MinIO (S3-compatible) with gateway to on-prem object store; keep a local delta CSI cache (rclone-cache or a small multi-AZ NFS backed by block PVs) for hot-models to avoid frequent object pulls.
- Tenant user data: encrypted block PVs (CSI driver: ceph-csi or csi-blockplugin), provisioned with QoS classes. Use LVM on host if you need live resizing without CSI support.
- Backups: snapshot-based backups to object store nightly; retention policy 30/90/365 per tenant classification.

Tenant isolation options (trade-offs):
- Cluster-per-tenant: best audit isolation, simpler egress controls, more overhead to manage multiple clusters. Good for PCI/PHI customers.
- Shared cluster, namespace isolation: better resource utilization, requires strict admission controllers, network policies, OPA/Gatekeeper policies, and per-namespace encryption keys. Add eBPF-based network observability.

Network/firewall notes for Redwood Private control plane:
- Persistent outbound to control-plane endpoints over TLS (443). We use mTLS tunnels for agent control - ephemeral outbound ports 10250 (kubelet) are required when behind strict NAT unless you use agent reverse-connect.
- KV cache replication: TCP 6379 (redis-compatible) or gRPC endpoints depending on chosen cache. Prefer a private peering route; avoid opening wide CIDR ranges.

I'll bring configuration snippets and PV class yaml examples to the call.
